'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Syrian civil war]]
**[[War against the Islamic State]]
***The [[United States Central Command]] announces that a [[General Atomics MQ-9 Reaper|MQ-9 Reaper]] [[drone warfare|drone strike]] killed a senior [[Islamic State]] leader, Usamah al-Muhajir, in eastern [[Syria]] two days ago. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/us-central-command-says-they-killed-isis-leader-usamah-al-mahajir-eastern-syria-2023-07-09/ (Reuters)]
**At least eight people are killed by two separate car bombings in northern Syria. [https://english.alarabiya.net/News/middle-east/2023/07/10/Several-car-bombings-shake-northern-Syria-leave-eight-dead (AFP via Al Arabiya)]
*[[Somali Civil War (2009–present)|Somali Civil War]]
**The [[United States Department of Defense]] announces that ten [[Al-Shabaab (militant group)|Al-Shabaab]] members were killed today by airstrikes near [[Afmadow]], [[Jubaland]], [[Somalia]]. [https://edition.cnn.com/2023/07/09/politics/somalia-al-shabaab-us-airstrikes/index.html (CNN)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*Fifteen people are killed by landslides and flooding across northern [[India]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/gallery/2023/7/9/photos-several-dead-as-heavy-rainfall-lashes-northern-india (Al Jazeera)]
*Ten people are killed and 30 others are injured when a bus falls off a bridge into a river in [[North Central Province, Sri Lanka|North Central Province]], [[Sri Lanka]]. [https://english.news.cn/20230710/ffb065073b894a958896233ccd546b4e/c.html (Xinhua)]
*Seven people are killed and twelve others are injured when a gas cylinder explosion causes a three-story building to collapse in [[Jhelum]], [[Punjab, Pakistan|Punjab]], [[Pakistan]]. [https://dunyanews.tv/en/Pakistan/738234-Death-toll-in-cylinder-explosion-in-Jhelum-rises-to-seven (Dunya News)]
*Three people are killed when a small [[Cessna]] [[plane crash]]es in [[Eastern Region (Iceland)|Eastern Region]], [[Iceland]]. [https://icelandmonitor.mbl.is/news/news/2023/07/10/three_people_died_in_an_airplane_crash/ (Iceland Monitor)]
*One person is killed and an unknown number of others are missing as a result of floods caused by torrential rains in [[Hudson Valley]], [[New York (state)|New York]], [[United States]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/2023/07/09/nyregion/flooding-west-point-orange-county.html (''The New York Times'')]
*A [[jet bridge]] collapses at the [[Dublin Airport]] in [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]], damaging an [[American Airlines]] [[Boeing 787]] aircraft. [https://www.irishtimes.com/ireland/dublin/2023/07/09/aircraft-damaged-at-dublin-airport-after-air-bridge-collapse/ (''Irish Times'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[New Zealand–European Union relations]]
**[[New Zealand]] signs a [[free trade agreement]] with the [[European Union]], which is expected to increase EU [[export]]s to the South Pacific nation by [[€]]4.5 billion a year. [https://www.rte.ie/news/business/2023/0709/1393622-new-zealand/ (AFP via RTÉ)]
*[[15th BRICS summit]]
**[[South African President]] [[Cyril Ramaphosa]] confirms that the upcoming [[BRICS]] [[Summit (meeting)|summit]] in [[Johannesburg]] will be conducted in-person for the first time since [[11th BRICS summit|2019]], despite an [[International Criminal Court]] [[International Criminal Court arrest warrants for Vladimir Putin and Maria Lvova-Belova|arrest warrant]] against [[President of Russia|Russian president]] [[Vladimir Putin]]. However, Ramaphosa does not state whether Putin will attend the summit. [https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2023/07/09/brics-summit-to-be-physical-despite-putin-warrant-south-africa-a81781 (AFP via ''The Moscow Times'')]
*[[Poland–Ukraine relations]]
**[[President of Poland]] [[Andrzej Duda]] and [[President of Ukraine]] [[Volodymyr Zelenskyy]] commemorate the victims of the [[Massacres of Poles in Volhynia and Eastern Galicia|1943 massacres in Volhynia and Eastern Galicia]] at a ceremony held at the [[Saint Peter and Paul Cathedral, Lutsk|Saint Peter and Paul Cathedral]] in [[Lutsk]], [[Ukraine]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/zelenskyy-duda-remember-wwii-volhynia-massacre-victims/a-66168573 (DW)]

'''Law and crime'''
*British [[public broadcaster]] [[BBC]] suspends a male [[Television presenter|presenter]] over allegations of [[sexual misconduct]] involving a [[Child sexual abuse|minor]], which the BBC first became aware of two months ago. [https://edition.cnn.com/2023/07/08/europe/bbc-presenter-sexual-misconduct-intl-hnk/index.html (CNN)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2023 Gabonese general election]]
**[[President of Gabon|President]] [[Ali Bongo Ondimba]] announces his bid for a third term in office. [https://guardian.ng/news/world/gabon-president-ali-bongo-says-will-run-for-third-term/ (AFP via ''The Guardian'')]
*[[2024 Salvadoran general election]]
**[[President of El Salvador|President]] [[Nayib Bukele]] formalizes his presidential re-election campaign with the [[Nuevas Ideas]] political party. [https://apnews.com/article/bukele-el-salvador-president-reelection-2739ba5508a1530939a84fa3e3cfc41a (AP)]
*[[2023 Uzbek presidential election]]
**[[Uzbekistan|Uzbeks]] vote for a [[President of Uzbekistan|president]] following the approval of the [[2023 Uzbek constitutional referendum|constitutional referendum]] which reset term limits, allowing incumbent president [[Shavkat Mirziyoyev]] to serve two more seven-year terms. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20230709-uzbekistan-holds-vote-set-to-cement-president-s-rule (AFP via France 24)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2023 LPGA Tour]]
**[[2023 U.S. Women's Open]]
***In [[golf]], American [[Allisen Corpuz]] wins the 78th [[U.S. Women's Open]] at the [[Pebble Beach Golf Links]] in [[Pebble Beach, California|Pebble Beach]], [[California]], [[United States]], after firing a three-under 69 to finish on nine under, three shots ahead of [[England]]'s [[Charley Hull]] and [[South Korea]]'s [[Jiyai Shin]]. [https://www.bbc.com/sport/golf/66151539 (BBC Sport)]
